transcript:
maya: hey team, running into a flake when deploying vector-worker -> KMS decrypt fails for pod shortly after helm upgrade. thinking it's an IRSA + kms grant ordering thing. anyone seen this pattern?
raj: yup, seen it. usually the svcacct role or the kms grant isn't fully propagated when pods start. what does your tf look like? are you creating a aws_kms_grant and the iam role in same apply?
maya: here's the relevant bits (simplified):

```hcl
resource "aws_iam_role" "vector_worker_irsa" {
  name = "vector-worker-irsa-${var.env}"
  assume_role_policy = data.aws_iam_policy_document.irsa.json
}

resource "helm_release" "vector_worker" {
  name       = "vector-worker"
  chart      = "./charts/vector"
  set { name = "serviceAccount.create" value = "false" }
  set { name = "serviceAccount.name" value = aws_iam_role.vector_worker_irsa.name }
}

resource "aws_kms_grant" "vector_decrypt" {
  key_id = aws_kms_key.secrets.id
  grantee_principal = aws_iam_role.vector_worker_irsa.arn
  operations = ["Decrypt"]
}
```

maya: I tried adding depends_on for the grant -> iam role but still flaky during CI deploys.
sam: two quick notes: 1) helm_release will create the k8s objects immediately during apply, 2) IAM role -> the IRSA binding uses the OIDC annotation on the k8s SA, not the role name. Are you using the aws-load-balancer-controller-ish pattern or eksctl style IRSA? need to confirm how SA maps to role.
maya: we annotate the SA with eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn = <role arn> in the chart. helm creates SA and pods start within seconds.
leah: infra observation: KMS grants are eventually consistent for cross-account/principal propagation sometimes. even if grant resource returns success, AWS backend might reject Decrypt for a short window. I've seen 30s-2m delays.
oliver: also watch STS session name / source identity. If you're relying on session tags or conditions in the key policy, the first assumption session may not have the expected attributes right away.
raj: i'd do one of two safe approaches: (A) move KMS grant out of same apply and run a short loop/wait after IAM role creation before helm_release; or (B) use key policy that allows the role principal (less fragile) and create grant as fallback. option A is simplest for now.
maya: for option A, any handy terraform pattern? I want to keep it in pipeline but ensure ordering w/o brittle sleeps.
sam: you can create a null_resource with local-exec that waits for a successful sts:DecodeAuthorizationMessage or a simple AWS CLI call that attempts decrypt of a test ciphertext (or kms:DescribeKey) using the new role via assume-role. then depends_on that before helm_release.

```hcl
resource "null_resource" "wait_kms_ready" {
  depends_on = [aws_kms_grant.vector_decrypt, aws_iam_role.vector_worker_irsa]

  provisioner "local-exec" {
    command = <<EOT
for i in {1..12}; do
  aws sts assume-role --role-arn ${aws_iam_role.vector_worker_irsa.arn} --role-session-name tf-check >/dev/null 2>&1 && break
  sleep 5
done
EOT
  }
}

resource "helm_release" "vector_worker" {
  depends_on = [null_resource.wait_kms_ready]
  # ...
}
```

leah: careful: CI runners need AWS creds that can assume-role. if pipeline can't assume the new role yet, that command will fail. you might instead call kms:Encrypt/Decrypt against the key as the new principal using temporary creds — but that's similar.
maya: good call. our pipeline runner can't assume the role until it's created; but it can call iam:SimulatePrincipalPolicy? hmm.
oliver: SimulatePrincipalPolicy could be used to check permissions but doesn't guarantee KMS grant propagation state. still, as a gate it's helpful.
raj: alternative: add a short pre/post hook in the helm chart that delays the pod start until annotation validated. e.g., an initContainer that loops on aws kms decrypt with the current pod's role creds; that way the pod will retry at start and succeed when grant propagates.
maya: i like the initContainer idea — keeps terraform simpler and retries per-pod.
sam: example initContainer (very rough):

```yaml
initContainers:
- name: kms-wait
  image: amazonlinux:2
  command: ["/bin/sh","-c","until aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb:///tmp/test.blob --key-id $KMS_KEY_ID >/dev/null 2>&1; do sleep 5; done"]
  env:
  - name: KMS_KEY_ID
    value: "arn:aws:kms:...:key/..."
```

leah: that will add 2-3s startup on success; but much better UX than random failures.
maya: ok i'll prototype initContainer + keep grant in tf. question: should aws_kms_grant use grantee_principal = data.aws_iam_role.vector_worker_irsa.arn or role ARN vs role ID matters?
raj: use the role ARN. grants accept principal ARN. avoid using role id.
oliver: also confirm key policy doesn't explicitly deny the role; grants are additive but key policy can block. if you have condition keys like aws:SourceAccount or aws:PrincipalOrgID that might cause rejection.
maya: thanks — quick followups: 1) i'll add initContainer, 2) will move null wait to pipeline if we need stronger gating, 3) i'll run an experiment to remove the grant and rely on key policy for role access to see stability.
sam: SGTM. ping here when you have the snippet, happy to review.
infra-bot: CI: terraform apply started for env=staging (run: #4567)
maya: thanks all, will attach snippets before EOD.
raj: if it helps, we also have a small library module under modules/kms that does an optional salt/wait logic — can point you to it.
maya: yes please raj, link would help. :thumbsup:
